old_value: The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <fresh scratch>

step_0_scenario_identification.claim: '120' in the scenario name is Syndra's splinter count at its maximum, not a build price or a duration.
step_0_scenario_identification.quote: P = 120-splinter +15% total AP BUFF ... splinters option (0-120) gates Q2 second charge, W 60-splinter true-damage (12%+2%/100 AP), P 120-splinter +15% AP capstone
step_0_scenario_identification.consequence: The scenario is Syndra at max splinters under a custom item order; the leaf sits in the utility-focus objective outcome, whose item_coverage list carries a per-item verdict + reason for items that contribute no outgoing damage.

step_1_the_operative_claim_both_strings_.claim: A mechanic that only alters the holder's durability contributes exactly 0 to outgoing TDD.
derivation: docs/math-foundations.md Sec.0: the deterministic scoring path emits T = E[ D | model, config ] -- one number, the expected damage the attacker deals.

docs/math-foundations.md Sec.1.1: D is assembled from the attacker's own event stream: N(T) = floor(AS * u * T) autos on a deterministic renewal schedule plus ability casts on one shared timeline. Every term is an attacker offence quantity (AD/AP, ratios, AS, cast times).
docs/math-foundations.md Sec.2.1: each term is then scaled by the TARGET's mitigation m(R) = 100/(100+R), with the negative branch m(R) = 2 - 100/(100-R).
docs/math-foundations.md Sec.2.2: the only resistance inputs are reduction/penetration applied to the TARGET's R (flat reduction -> % reduction -> % penetration -> flat penetration).
step_1_the_operative_claim_both_strings_.conclusion: The holder's armour, magic resistance, health, self-shields, spell shields, damage-taken reduction and stasis appear in NO term of D. d(TDD)/d(holder durability) = 0 identically. Both the old and the new string assert this, and the assertion is TRUE.

house_precedent.quote: P (Blast Shield - defensive shield, does not change outgoing TDD) ... P Blast Shield is explicitly documented as defensive-only ('does not change outgoing TDD').
house_precedent.note: 'defensive -> does not change outgoing TDD' is the repo's established sourced-boundary language, so neither string is inventing a category.

step_2_the_material_difference.difference: The new string prepends the ANTECEDENT that licenses the conclusion ('Every declared family on this item is a defence'); the old string states only the CONSEQUENT.
step_2_the_material_difference.test: Is that guard load-bearing, or decoration? Checked against the cached wiki text for every shop-defensive item, because if some defence-tagged item does deal damage, the unguarded sentence is a false statement waiting to be emitted.

counterexamples_found_in_cache.passive_text: Thorns - When struck by a basic attack on-hit, deal 20 (+ 10% bonus armor) magic damage to the attacker and, if they are a champion, inflict them with Grievous Wounds for 3 seconds.
counterexamples_found_in_cache.why_it_matters: A pure-defence stat line whose represented mechanic emits magic damage scaling off a DEFENSIVE stat. 'The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD' is simply false here.

counterexamples_found_in_cache.passive_text: Immolate - Taking or dealing damage activates this passive for 3 seconds. Deal 20 (+ 1% bonus health) magic damage every second to enemies within 325 (+ 100% bonus ...) units.
counterexamples_found_in_cache.why_it_matters: Damage-per-second scaling off bonus health -- durability stat, offensive output.

counterexamples_found_in_cache.passive_text: Immolate - ... Deal 15 (+ 1% bonus health) magic damage every second ...; Desolate - Killing a non-champion unit causes an eruption ...
counterexamples_found_in_cache.why_it_matters: Same shape on the MR side.

counterexamples_found_in_cache.passive_text: Unmake - Enemy champions within 700 units of you become cursed, causing them to receive 12% increased magic damage from all sources.
counterexamples_found_in_cache.why_it_matters: A tank item that is a straight OUTGOING-damage amplifier; declares the damage family in data/item-atoms/8020.json (['damage','stats']).

step_2_the_material_difference.conclusion: The guard is load-bearing. The new sentence's antecedent is FALSE for Thornmail / Sunfire / Hollow Radiance / Abyssal Mask, so the sentence cannot be emitted for them; the old sentence has no antecedent and would assert a falsehood if the coverage classifier ever routed one of these items to this branch. The new string is the sound form -- it states the condition under which its conclusion holds.

step_3_the_new_antecedent_is_satisfiable.purpose: Confirm the new sentence is not vacuous or unsatisfiable -- there really are items whose every declared effect family is defensive.
step_3_the_new_antecedent_is_satisfiable.method: Grouped data/item-atoms/*.json by the non-stat 'family' labels each item declares.

worked_example_mage_utility_pool.sole_declared_effect: Annul - Grants a spell shield that blocks the next hostile ability (40 second cooldown, timer restarts upon taking damage from champions).
worked_example_mage_utility_pool.reading: One mechanic, one family, purely defensive: it absorbs one inbound ability. Substituting into the Sec.1.1/2.1 damage identity changes nothing on the attacker side -> 0 contribution to outgoing TDD. Both antecedent and consequent of the new string hold.

sibling_examples: Kaenic Rookern (2504) - Magebane: 'After not taking magic damage for 15 seconds, gain a shield that absorbs magic damage equal to 15% of maximum health until destroyed.' Pure durability.
Verdant Barrier (4632) - Annul, the EPIC component of Banshee's, same single defensive family.

step_4_terminology_check.defence_vs_durability: 'Defence' in LoL usage denotes armour/magic resistance specifically; 'durability' is the superset that also covers maximum health, shields, spell shields and damage-taken reduction. Every worked example above (spell shield, %max-HP shield, heal/shield amplification, stasis) is durability but not strictly armour/MR, so 'changes durability' is the STRICTLY more accurate consequent. The new wording is not a loss of precision.
step_4_terminology_check.TDD: outgoing Total Damage Dealt = the T of docs/math-foundations.md Sec.0. Used identically in both strings.

residual_uncertainty.what_i_could_not_pin: The identity of item_coverage[0] itself. The scenario tuple for 'syndra_custom_order_120' is defined under scripts/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids me to read; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json holds 22 corpus scenarios and none is a Syndra scenario, so the build order is not recoverable from the permitted evidence tree.
residual_uncertainty.why_the_verdict_still_holds: The adjudication does not depend on which item it is. For ANY item that can legitimately reach this branch, the new string is true (verified above for the whole class of single-defensive-family items). For any item that CANNOT legitimately reach it (Thornmail, Sunfire, Hollow Radiance, Abyssal Mask), the new string's antecedent blocks it while the old string would state a falsehood. There is no item in data/items.json for which the old string is true and the new string is false.
residual_uncertainty.scope_caveat_applying_equally_to_both_st: Both strings scope to 'the represented mechanic', NOT to the item's stat line. That scoping is necessary and is preserved in the new wording: Banshee's Veil carries 105 ability power, which very much does change Syndra's outgoing TDD through the stats layer (and is further amplified by her 120-splinter +15% total AP capstone, data/champion-audit/batch-6.json). Read as a claim about the item's effect/family coverage it is correct; read as a claim about the whole item it would be wrong -- for the old string as much as the new one, so it does not separate them.
residual_uncertainty.one_genuine_modelling_boundary_noted_in_: If item_coverage[0] were Zhonya's Hourglass (3157), note that Time Stop's cached text says the holder is 'unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items' for 2.5 seconds -- in a fixed-length fight window that strictly REDUCES outgoing TDD via the Sec.1.1 renewal count N(T) = floor(AS*u*T). That is a documented-boundary question about the fight model, it applies identically to both the old and the new wording, and it does not flip this verdict.

conclusion: Both strings assert the same true consequent (a durability-only mechanic contributes 0 to outgoing TDD, an identity that follows directly from the Sec.0/1.1/2.1 damage composition, where no holder-side defensive quantity appears). The new string additionally states the antecedent that licenses it, and the cached item data shows that antecedent is load-bearing rather than decorative: four shop-defensive items in data/items.json (Thornmail, Sunfire Aegis, Hollow Radiance, Abyssal Mask) do change outgoing TDD, and only the new wording excludes them. 'Durability' is also the strictly more accurate term than 'defence' for spell shields, %max-HP shields and heal/shield amplification. No item in the cache makes the old string true and the new string false.
